3.0.0.en: The responsibilities of the bishop are great, because he bears the responsibility of leading the Church, and he is exposed to persecutions and troubles from outside and from within. So St. Paul declares that whoever loves God and desires to consecrate his life to Him in the service of the priesthood, this is a good thing that gladdens God’s heart. It is to be noted that he mentioned the qualifications of the bishop and then the qualifications of the deacon, because by “bishop” he means the priesthood in general, that is, the bishop and the priest.

3.1.0.en: St. Paul makes clear the qualities that must be found in him, which are:

3.1.1.en: Blameless: that is, without clear sins that cause others to stumble; he does not mean any sin in the heart, because there is no person without sin.

3.1.2.en: The husband of one wife: married once, or not married again after being widowed; this declares his chastity by being content with a single marriage.

3.1.3.en: Vigilant: alert, watchful, cautious, of keen insight, mindful of the salvation of his own soul and of those he shepherds. Sober: steady, acting with wisdom and moderation.

3.1.4.en: Of good behaviour: modest in his appearance, his conduct and his speech, keeping away from frivolity.

3.1.5.en: Given to hospitality: hosting strangers is a sign of a wide heart. In the early Christian period the believers moved about much because of persecution, and therefore the bishop’s house had to be open to them.

3.1.6.en: Apt to teach: he has the gift of teaching, founded on right spiritual knowledge.

3.2.0.en: Not given to wine: wine is not forbidden, but there is no need for it. What is forbidden is excessive drinking that leads to drunkenness, and this is of course a quality rejected in a bishop, and it means not being absorbed in general in the enjoyment of food and drink.

3.2.1.en: No striker: that is, one who strikes often and is quick to use it as a means of correcting those who are spiritually deviant. Not greedy of filthy lucre: not a lover of money, especially what he gets through improper conduct, such as giving up what is right to please some of the rich; rather, money is only a means for service and for supporting the needy, and he does not care whether he has it or not.

3.2.2.en: Patient: patient with his spiritual children, not flaring up at their mistakes but bringing them back to the truth with all patience.

3.2.3.en: Not a brawler: he does not break the bond of affection and relationship with any of his children, whatever the reasons. Not covetous: the love of money is the root of all evil, so it is not fitting that it should possess the heart of the bishop, who is supposed to be an example of goodness.

3.3.0.en: He leads and manages his house soundly and brings up his children well, so that they obey him and submit to the Christian teachings and principles that he teaches them.

3.4.0.en: Whoever cannot give heed to his children and care for them as he ought will not be able to do this in the wider circle, which is the church of God.

3.5.0.en: Not a novice: not one who has believed only a short while.

3.5.1.en: Lifted up with pride: that is, becoming arrogant.

3.5.2.en: The condemnation of the devil: he falls into many sins for which Satan accuses him before God. The Apostle warns against being hasty in ordaining a person who began to attach himself to the Church and to serve only a short time ago, because by this he is exposed to pride, thinking himself better than those who preceded him in the Church, and this creates many problems.

3.6.0.en: The bishop must have a good reputation, and his goodness must be clear and his former conduct above reproach, so that Satan does not use his enemies or unbelievers to condemn and blame him.

3.6.1.en: These qualifications apply to every servant and every spiritual person, so examine yourself on the basis of these qualities and strive to acquire the one you find you need most.

3.7.0.en: The deacons: what is meant here is the full deacon, that is, the diaconos, and not the preliminary ranks such as reader and chanter, in which most deacons are ordained at present.

3.7.1.en: As the Apostle specified in the previous verses the qualities that must be found in the bishop, here he specifies them for the candidates for the diaconate, which are:

3.7.2.en: That they be grave: that is, of refined, steady conduct.

3.7.3.en: Not doubletongued: that they not be deceitful.

3.7.4.en: Not given to much wine: this is the same quality required in the bishop and mentioned in (v. 3). Not greedy of filthy lucre: this too was mentioned before in (v. 3).

3.8.0.en: The mystery of the faith: Christ the Savior of the whole world, Jews and Gentiles, whatever their sins; it is called a mystery because the love of Christ the Savior surpasses intellectual comprehension.

3.8.1.en: The deacon must have strong faith with a pure conscience, that is, sincerity without personal aim.

3.9.0.en: Before deacons are ordained, they must first be proved by serving faithfully and lovingly, and their conduct in their former and present life is likewise proved. If the result of the proving is positive, which St. Paul expresses by the phrase “blameless,” they are then qualified for the rank of deacon.

3.10.0.en: The discourse here does not concern women in general, but concerns deaconesses or consecrated women or the wives of deacons, and the qualities required in them are as follows:

3.10.1.en: Grave: as mentioned in the qualities of deacons and priests.

3.10.2.en: Not slanderers: they do not speak of the faults of others.

3.10.3.en: Sober: mindful of their spiritual life.

3.10.4.en: Faithful in all things: sincere, for by their position they are privy to the secrets of homes, so they must be faithful with the secrets entrusted to them, faithful in distributing alms, faithful in the holy commandments.

3.12.0.en: The Apostle shows the blessing of the service of the diaconate, which helps the one who holds it to grow in faith in Christ through his service.

3.12.1.en: The place, the work and the circumstances that God has given you, whether you are a servant in the Church or a father or a mother, be faithful in them and ask God’s help to glorify Him through them.

3.13.0.en: St. Paul promises Timothy to come to him, in order to reassure him and encourage him and affirm to him that, as he has guided and directed him by this epistle, he will support him by his personal presence with him in Ephesus.

3.14.0.en: Behave thyself: manage the Church and lead the ministry in it.

3.14.1.en: The pillar and ground of the truth: the support of the truth, for the Church, by the strong faith in Christ within her, proclaims and supports the truth in the whole world.

3.14.2.en: The Apostle affirms to his disciple Timothy that he will come to him, but if he is delayed in coming he should not be distressed, because this will be by the permission of the Holy Spirit, so that Timothy may have more opportunity to work and to exert more effort as a servant of the church of the living God, which the Apostle calls the house of God. And he defined the features of the Church as resting on the truth, which is the foundation of faith, and not relying on knowledge as the foundation of salvation, as the Gnostic heretics claim.

3.15.0.en: The Church is not merely theoretical knowledge about God, as the Gnostics imagined, which made them fall into false knowledge of Him, but she is a practical faith that appears in a life filled with righteousness and goodness, which we call the godly life, which is a great mystery that appeared in practice in the life of Christ on earth, and the verse shows it in the following stages:

3.15.1.en: (1) God was manifest in the flesh: the Second Hypostasis became incarnate, becoming in the likeness of men. This is a clear verse proving the divinity of Christ.

3.15.2.en: (2) Justified in the Spirit: the Holy Spirit bore witness to His righteousness.

3.15.3.en: (3) Seen of angels: the angels saw Him with us during His incarnation.

3.15.4.en: (4) Preached unto the Gentiles: the Messiah the Savior was proclaimed among the Gentiles and not among the Jews only. (5) Believed on in the world: all enjoy faith without favoring one nation over another. (6) Received up into glory: He ascended to heavenly glory.

3.15.5.en: Your steadfastness in the Church is steadfastness in the truth, so you live reassured and secure your eternity. So take care to attend the Church and to enjoy her Holy Sacraments, and submit to her teachings even if they conflict with some of your thoughts or personal aims.

3.15.6.en: Spiritual discipleship and rejecting the teachings of the heretics

4.0.s.en: (1) Rejecting the words of the heretics

4.0.0.en: The Holy Spirit teaches the prophets about future matters, and so St. Paul taught clearly and prophesied that in the latter times, by which he means the times that extend from Christ’s ascension to His Second Coming, people will depart from the right faith delivered to the saints and follow the demons, who lead them astray from the way of Christ.

4.1.0.en: Seared: burned with fire like skin, so that it loses its feeling; the meaning is that their consciences lose their feeling as if seared with a hot iron.

4.1.1.en: These deviant people will deceive the simple by acting out the godly life, while their consciences have lost all sense of responsibility, so they proclaim false teachings.

4.2.0.en: The heretics (the Gnostics and the followers of Mani) proclaimed abstaining from marriage, considering marital relations unclean, and they held that it is not fitting for the perfect to partake of meats and some other foods. But Christians believe in the holiness of marriage and bodily relations, and that all foods are a gift from God, so they eat them with thanksgiving.

4.3.0.en: We believe that God made everything good (Gen 1:31), and there is nothing unclean in His creation, and before we eat we pray and remember God’s blessing of the foods as it is written in the Holy Bible, then we eat and give thanks to God.

4.4.0.en: The good shepherd is the one who speaks to the flock and reminds them of the right truths of the faith that they have already learned. By your commitment to this reminding of the believers, you will be a good minister of Jesus Christ, since you were brought up in the right faith and sound teachings, far from deceptions.

4.5.0.en: Profane and old wives’ fables: pagan or Jewish ideas that the elderly pass on from their fathers, all of which are false and trivial matters that occupy a person and hinder him from his spiritual life, that is, they defile his mind with worthless thoughts.

4.5.1.en: Exercise thyself: strive by spiritual exercises to grow in virtue.

4.5.2.en: The Apostle warns Timothy not to be occupied with the ideas of pagans or Jews that are far from the truth, and to care for his goal, which is the spiritual life, and so to train himself to grow in it.

4.6.0.en: That which is to come: eternal life.

4.6.1.en: Bodily exercise profits only the body, but godliness and the fear of God profit the whole being of man, that is, spirit and body together, for they purify his body, sanctify his thought, direct his will to the good and prepare him for eternal life.

4.6.2.en: Society may convey wrong ideas to you, so examine everything: does it agree with your faith and the teachings of the Church or not? And do not be distracted from your goal, which is the love of God, and so you advance at all times.

4.7.0.en: The faithful saying, worthy of all acceptation, is that godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come; it gives hope in the present life and leads to a happy eternal life.

4.8.0.en: The believer bears toil and insult for the sake of holding fast to the godly life, but his hope in Christ, who upholds him in afflictions, comforts his heart, because God upholds everyone who takes refuge in Him in affliction, and especially the believers.

4.9.0.en: He charges Timothy to teach the people all that has gone before in this chapter.

4.9.1.en: To the degree that you look to God, you can face afflictions and bear them, for He will uphold you and lighten them for you when you feel His presence with you, and in the end He will reward you with inexpressible blessings. So always remember that God is with you and does not leave you as long as you want Him.

4.10.0.en: Here St. Paul gives his disciple Timothy commandments that touch his spiritual striving, which are: Let no man despise thy youth: Timothy was young in age at the beginning of his episcopate, so the Apostle encourages him not to be concerned about this, since the power of Christ is with him and he carries out his pastoral ministry with confidence. An example in word: so that the words of God appear on his lips and his manner, being steady and precise. In conversation: his conduct is to be Christian according to God’s commandments.

4.10.1.en: In charity: his love for all appears, especially for those who wrong him.

4.10.2.en: In spirit: his spirituality appears in his worship and conduct.

4.10.3.en: In faith: in his teachings and in the face of difficult situations and afflictions.

4.10.4.en: In purity: the purity of his words and conduct from every evil aim.

4.11.0.en: He charges Timothy to care for reading the Holy Bible and meditating on it, the effect of which will appear in his preaching and teaching of the people, and to persevere in this until he meets Paul, who will complete his teaching and guidance.

4.12.0.en: The gift: the grace of the sacrament of the priesthood with all the gifts it carries, such as preaching and teaching.

4.12.1.en: Prophecy: there was a prophecy about Timothy that he would become a bishop and shepherd of God’s people. The laying on of the hands of the presbytery: when he was ordained bishop, Paul and the bishops with him laid their hands on him. This shows that ordination to the priesthood is by the laying on of the bishops’ hands on those presented for this rank. He calls him to use the gifts of God given to him in the priesthood, which God confirmed beforehand by prophecy, so that he may enjoy the work of God and benefit all those he shepherds.

4.13.0.en: He charges him to care for his ministry and to be wholly in it, that is, not to be occupied with any other works because he is consecrated to God, and by this he advances in his spiritual life and his ministry.

4.14.0.en: He also charges him with spiritual discipleship and constant learning from the Holy Bible and the teachings of the Apostle to him and benefiting from all people, and to the degree of his care for learning he will gain the salvation of his own soul and the salvation of the souls of those he shepherds.

4.14.1.en: If the bishop needs to continue in discipleship, reading and learning all the days of his life, then all the more do you need this, whatever your age or experience, because by this humility and your seeking the knowledge of God, He works in you by His Holy Spirit and guides you, so you delight in fellowship with Him, and those around you learn from your spirituality and come to God. So care not only for reading but also for observing the virtues of others, even children, so that you learn from every person.

4.14.2.en: Commandments for the elders, the widows and the priests

5.0.s.en: (1) Treatment of the elderly and the young

5.0.0.en: The Apostle warns the shepherd Timothy to be wise in his dealing with every category of the flock, for shepherds are fathers responsible for all the people.

5.0.1.en: Rebuke not an elder: respecting the elderly and not reproving them harshly, but exhorting them as fathers who deserve honor for their age.

5.0.2.en: The younger men as brethren: the bishop’s humility appears not only with the elders but also with the young, so he treats them and teaches them as his brothers.

5.0.3.en: The elder women as mothers: treating and teaching elderly women as his mothers, with sufficient esteem and respect.

5.0.4.en: The younger as sisters: treating young women also with humility as his sisters, taking care over purity of heart, speech and conduct.

5.0.5.en: In your dealing with others, take care to honor the elderly and everyone who holds a position or has experience, for by this humility of yours you win everyone and learn from them, and you can draw them to Christ, and they esteem your words.

5.1.1.en: Widows indeed: those who have no one to support them.

5.1.2.en: The Apostle directs Timothy’s attention to caring for widows who are in material need, providing for their needs.

5.2.0.en: The Apostle requires the believer whose mother or grandmother has been widowed to be committed to supporting her, for she is the one who served him and raised him in his childhood and youth. If she has become unable to provide for her needs because of her old age and the absence of anyone to support her, he must care for her in return for the toil she endured in raising him, for if he does so he does what is good and acceptable before God.

5.3.0.en: The Apostle stipulated that the one whom the Church helps must have no children or grandchildren able to support her, and that she has set her hope on the one who is truly able to support, and believes that God will not leave her alone, and continues in supplications and prayers without ceasing.

5.4.0.en: The widow absorbed in material things and in needless luxury is distracted from God by such conduct, so she dies spiritually.

5.5.0.en: Timothy, as a shepherd, is required to charge the widows to be in constant vigilance and to keep away from sin.

5.6.0.en: The believer is committed not only toward his mother or grandmother who is a widow, but toward the wider circle of those around him of relatives, especially his family, that is, those of his own house. For true faith moves a person toward love of others and care for them, especially those of his own house. And whoever does not behave so has denied the faith in practice in his life, and in this way becomes worse than an unbeliever, because even the pagan performs such duties toward his family and needy relatives.

5.7.0.en: The Apostle specified the conditions necessary for choosing the widow deaconess, which are:

5.7.1.en: Not under threescore years old: so that no one stumbles at her moving among the homes of those served and accompanying the priests when they visit some homes.

5.7.2.en: The wife of one man: she must not have been married more than once, as a proof of chastity and purity. This is the same condition that was followed with the bishop anciently and with the priest or full deacon to this day. Well reported of for good works: she has a witness from others to her practice of the virtues and her attachment to good works that show a heart wide in love for others.

5.7.4.en: If she have brought up children: her motherhood appeared in raising her children, or any children if she has no children in the flesh, with evident care and attention.

5.7.5.en: If she have lodged strangers: she cared for those who have no one with whom to stay, and welcomed any person who was a stranger to the Church in order to encourage him and provide for his needs.

5.7.6.en: If she have washed the saints’ feet: washing the feet of the believers as was the custom anciently when they entered homes, where their feet were soiled with dust from walking in open sandals. And not only this, but offering all services with humility however lowly these services may seem, such as cleaning the church and helping every needy person, sick person and bedridden person.

5.7.7.en: If she have relieved the afflicted: whether in troubles or in prisons, by meeting their needs and encouraging them.

5.7.8.en: If she have diligently followed every good work: she cared for works of goodness.

5.8.0.en: They have begun to wax wanton against Christ: they were distracted from Christ by the world and material things.

5.8.1.en: Young widows should not be consecrated for service, for the Apostle fears that after consecrating their lives to Christ they will turn back and want to marry, and so their covenant will be broken, and thus they become sinners and condemned before God for going back on their first covenant after pledging themselves to consecration to the service of the Lord.

5.9.0.en: Because these widows are not occupied with Christ and His service, their time becomes empty, so they go about from house to house, multiplying words and searching for the news of people and spending long time in frivolity.

5.10.0.en: I will therefore that the younger women marry, instead of idleness and not being occupied with service, so that they bear children and care for their little ones. Marriage is not forbidden, but is a fortress for them, so that no room is left for Satan to blaspheme God because of them. For God is not dishonored by the marriage of widows, but by their idleness and inner emptiness. And she who cannot occupy her time with raising her children and serving the Church is liable to turn away from Christ by falling into many sins, so in this case marriage is better for chastity than widowhood.

5.10.1.en: This does not mean that young widows must marry, because chastity and being occupied with Christ are better.

5.11.0.en: Here St. Paul returns to affirm the commitment of families to their widows: the Church is committed to give to the needy women who have no one to support them, while leaving the affairs of the needy women who do have someone to support them in the hands of their relatives who are able.

5.11.1.en: May you care for the needy among your relatives, not only materially but rather spiritually, so that you care for the salvation of those around you and invite them to attend the Church and enjoy the Holy Sacraments, and pray for them always.

5.12.s.en: (3) Supporting the priests, trying them and ordaining them, with a special charge to Timothy

5.12.0.en: The elders: the correct translation here is “the priests.”

5.12.1.en: The Church is committed to meeting the material needs of the fathers the priests, so that they may devote themselves to preaching and teaching and not be burdened by the necessities of life. If the priests manage the spiritual affairs of the believers for their salvation, they must not be deprived of receiving their share of material needs, not that they may live in luxury but that they may have a decent living.

5.13.0.en: This commandment came in the book of Deuteronomy (Deut 25:4); it is a figurative picture saying that when the ox draws the threshing implement, it should not be muzzled, so that it may fill its belly from the fruit of its labor. So also the minister: it is his right that his bodily needs be met by those he serves. And the Apostle quotes in this regard the saying of the Lord Christ in (Lk 10:7) that “the labourer is worthy of his hire.”

5.14.0.en: An elder: what is meant by it here is the priest of the Church.

5.14.1.en: The Mosaic law required that no person be condemned without the testimony of two or three witnesses. Therefore the bishop should not be hasty in judging any priest, and should examine the complaint well.

5.15.0.en: The Apostle asks his disciple Timothy, concerning those against whom the accusations are proved and were serious for the faith of the people, to rebuke them before the whole Church in order to preserve the soundness of the Church’s faith.

5.16.0.en: In view of the priest’s standing and his influence on the people, St. Paul charges him before the Father and the Son and the holy angels not to give a judgment tainted by partiality or by bias to one side at the expense of the other, or with the aim of fulfilling personal desires.

5.17.0.en: He advises him not to ordain a priest hastily, but to examine him well, because he is responsible for the ordination of everyone he ordains. If there are faults in him that make others stumble, he shares in his faults by ordaining him, so he warns him to keep himself pure by not taking part in ordaining others who are unsuitable for the ranks of the priesthood.

5.17.1.en: Beware of haste in your judgment of others, especially if they hold a position or great responsibility. If the matter does not concern you, do not interfere in it, and if it is necessary for you to take a position and a decision, examine the matter well, and prayer will support you and guide you to good thought and conduct.

5.18.0.en: In consideration of Timothy’s illness, and out of St. Paul’s tenderness toward his sick disciple, he allowed him to drink a little wine as a remedy and not for pleasure. Here Paul’s fatherhood and his care for his son appear, not only in spiritual matters but also in bodily ones.

5.19.0.en: Open beforehand: known to the general public.

5.19.1.en: Going before to judgment: deserving the Church’s judgment upon them.

5.19.2.en: And some men they follow after: their sins are not apparent and are hidden in their hearts, but God judges them, and they too are not fit for the priesthood.

5.19.3.en: In choosing priests, Paul charges Timothy not to ordain those who have sins apparent to people and deserving ecclesiastical punishment, and likewise those whose sins do not appear but are hidden in their hearts, by examining them carefully, because good works are plain before people, and so are evil works; whoever has good works he chooses for the priesthood, but whoever has evil works he rejects.
